title: invariant on Enums
concept: Invariants can be applied to enum types to validate that each variant's data satisfies constraints — keeping discriminated unions safe.
why: Enums with data are powerful but dangerous without validation. Invariants ensure every variant's payload is valid, regardless of which variant is active.
tips: Match on the enum in the invariant to validate each variant's data
Use guards in the match to express complex per-variant constraints
Enum invariants protect against invalid payloads set via pattern matching reassignment
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle all variants in the invariant match — must be exhaustive
Writing per-variant checks that reference fields accessible only in other variants
Assuming enum variants are always valid — without invariants, any variant can hold garbage
